nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that distinguishes genuine utterance ambiguity from model uncertainty under unseen compositional structures.
requirements: Achieve ambiguity-detection F1 ≥0.85 on unseen compositions, using independently annotated sets of valid interpretations.
Match unambiguous-input execution accuracy of a single-output parser trained on identical data.

nodes.content: Freeze a single-output execution parser; train a set-valued validity head to flag multiple supported interpretations, separating ambiguity from ensemble disagreement.
How can the validity head recognize multiple licensed parses under unseen compositions without treating low-confidence alternatives as genuine ambiguity?
Set-supervised validity scores trained with compositional counterfactual negatives reject ensemble-only alternatives, achieving ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 without degrading frozen-decoder execution.
Train validity head on annotated interpretation sets and counterfactual negatives; calibrate on development compositions, evaluate unseen-composition F1 and execution parity.
Evaluate validity heads with and without counterfactual negatives on independently annotated CompSplit-1; measure ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution parity.
On CompSplit-1, counterfactual negatives raised ambiguity F1 from 0.78 to 0.87; frozen-decoder unambiguous execution matched baseline at 91%.
Adopt the counterfactual-trained validity head with frozen decoder: CompSplit-1 ambiguity F1 reached 0.87 while unambiguous execution remained 91%.
CompSplit-1 evaluation report records ablation F1 (0.78 versus 0.87), independent-annotation provenance, and 91% unambiguous execution parity.
Does the frozen parser’s candidate beam omit valid interpretations, causing missed ambiguity on unseen compositions?
Expanding the frozen parser’s beam from 8 to 32 raises valid-interpretation recall ≥5 points without changing top-1 execution.
Using the CompSplit-1 report’s annotation provenance and baseline, compare beams 8 and 32 on valid-interpretation recall and top-1 execution.
On unseen CompSplit-2, the same counterfactual-trained head scored beam-8 F1 0.82; beam-32 raised interpretation recall 79→86%, preserving 91% execution.
Beam-32 coverage plus counterfactual-trained validity calibration should distinguish genuine CompSplit-2 ambiguity from uncertainty (F1 ≥0.85), preserving 91% execution.
Calibrate beam-32 validity on development compositions; measure ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution against 91% on independently annotated CompSplit-2.
On CompSplit-2, calibrated beam-32 ambiguity F1 reached 0.86 versus beam-8’s 0.82; unambiguous execution remained 91%.
Use a typed compositional grammar to enumerate licensed parses and ensemble-stability tests to reject uncertainty, preserving baseline top-1 execution.
Induce a typed grammar, enumerate licensed parses, and test cross-seed stability; compare CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1 and 91% execution baseline.
Using CompSplit-1 report’s annotation provenance and baseline, induce a typed grammar; evaluate CompSplit-2 ambiguity F1, five-seed stability, and execution.
TypedGrammar-v1 contains induced type rules, enumerated CompSplit-2 parses, five-seed stability logs, and ambiguity F1 and execution scoring scripts.
Evaluate TypedGrammar-v1 against the counterfactual-trained beam-32 head on CompSplit-2, scoring ambiguity F1, five-seed stability, and unambiguous execution.
Across five CompSplit-2 seeds, TypedGrammar-v1 averaged ambiguity F1 0.87 versus beam-32’s 0.83 despite its earlier 0.86; both preserved 91% execution.
Select TypedGrammar-v1 for robustness: five-seed F1 averaged 0.87 versus beam-32’s 0.83 despite its earlier 0.86; execution stayed 91%.
Stress-test TypedGrammar-v1 on independently annotated CompSplit-3 depth-four compositions, recording valid-parse coverage, ambiguity F1, and unambiguous execution.
On CompSplit-3 depth-four cases, TypedGrammar-v1 covered 72% of valid parses and scored ambiguity F1 0.79, despite 91% execution.
Which missing typed composition rules account for TypedGrammar-v1’s 72% valid-parse coverage on depth-four CompSplit-3?
Adding quantified-relative-clause scope-lifting rules recovers ≥50% of missing CompSplit-3 parses, raising coverage from 72% to ≥85%.
Implement quantified-relative-clause scope-lifting in TypedGrammar-v1; test whether CompSplit-3 missing-parse recovery reaches 50% and coverage reaches 85%.
Scope-lifting recovered 54% of previously missing CompSplit-3 parses, raising valid-parse coverage from 72% to 87%.
Rerun CompSplit-3 ambiguity detection with scope-lifting enabled; measure F1 and unambiguous execution against TypedGrammar-v1’s 0.79 and 91%.
Independent re-adjudication corrected CompSplit-3 scope-lifting coverage from 87% to 80%; ambiguity F1 fell from 0.79 to 0.76, execution remained 91%.
Type-constrained scope lifting and coordinated-relative attachment should recover missing CompSplit-3 parses without spurious ambiguity, yielding coverage ≥85% and F1 ≥0.85.
Implement type-constrained scope lifting and coordinated-relative attachment; ablate each on re-adjudicated CompSplit-3, measuring coverage, ambiguity F1, and execution.
On re-adjudicated CompSplit-3, combined rules reached 88% valid-parse coverage and 0.86 ambiguity F1 versus 0.81/0.83 single-rule F1; execution remained 91%.
Adopt combined rules: scope lifting’s initial 87% coverage corrected to 80%; combined reached 88% coverage, 0.86 F1, and 91% execution.
Construct contrastive execution worlds for candidate logical forms and require paraphrase-consistent support for each interpretation; retain baseline top-1 execution.
Can contrastive worlds expose distinct valid interpretations when candidate logical forms execute identically on the original world?
Minimal world edits that separate candidate denotations reveal ≥90% of independently annotated interpretation pairs hidden by original-world equivalence.
Generate minimal world edits for original-world-equivalent CompSplit-3 parses; test annotated-pair separation and paraphrase consistency against random edits.
On CompSplit-3, generate minimal and random world edits for equivalent annotated parse pairs; compare separation recall and paraphrase consistency.
CompSplit-3 minimal edits separated 93% of equivalent annotated pairs versus 61% for random edits; paraphrase agreement was 89%.
WorldContrast-v1 contains minimal CompSplit-3 world edits, separated parse-pair labels, random-edit controls, and paraphrase-agreement scores.
Audit WorldContrast-v1 edits, then filter candidates by world separation and paraphrase support; measure CompSplit-3 ambiguity F1 and execution parity.
WorldContrast-v1 filtering achieved CompSplit-3 ambiguity F1 of 0.88 versus combined grammar’s 0.86; unambiguous execution remained 91%.
Generate targeted clarification questions; flag ambiguity when answer-conditioned parses receive independent support, while preserving the frozen execution decoder.
Train clarification-question generator on annotated parse distinctions; validate answer-conditioned support on unseen CompSplit-3, measuring ambiguity F1 and execution parity.
Train clarification questions on CompSplit-1/2 distinctions; use adopted combined-rule parses and WorldContrast-v1 worlds to evaluate CompSplit-3 interpretation support.
ClarifySplit-v1 contains generated CompSplit-3 clarification questions, answer-conditioned parse scores, and links to combined-rule parses and WorldContrast-v1 worlds.
Audit ClarifySplit-v1 parse support against independent annotations; compare clarification gating with WorldContrast-v1 on CompSplit-3 ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution.
On CompSplit-3, clarification gating scored ambiguity F1 0.89 versus WorldContrast-v1’s 0.88; both retained 91% unambiguous execution.
Select clarification gating: CompSplit-3 F1 0.89 beats world contrasts’ 0.88, repaired grammar’s 0.86, and previously selected grammar’s 0.79.
